desc:
Rewrite the array nums so that every 0 is written twice in a row. All other elements keep their order and shift to the right to make room. The array keeps its original length, so elements pushed past the end are simply dropped.

Return the resulting array (same length as nums). Aim for O(1) extra space.

nums = [1, 0, 2, 3, 0, 4, 5, 0]
result = [1, 0, 0, 2, 3, 0, 0, 4]
hints: Building a new longer list and cutting it to the original length works. Can you avoid the extra list?
Writing from the front would overwrite elements you have not read yet. Which direction is safe?

Count the zeros first, so you know where the last element ends up if the array were long enough. Then walk from the back with a read index and a write index, and write only when the write index is inside the array.
editorial: Imagine the fully expanded array of length n + zeros. Every element of the original has a known final position there, and the real array is just its first n cells.

Walk i from the end of nums backwards with a write pointer j that starts at n + zeros - 1. Copy nums[i] to j if j < n, then move j down; if the element is a zero, write one more zero at the new j (again only if inside the array) and move j down again. Because j ≥ i at all times, no unread value is overwritten.
One pass to count and one pass to write give O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
